title: Disney Gave Kingdom Hearts One Scene With Mickey
hook:
Disney's contract let the first Kingdom Hearts use Mickey Mouse in exactly one scene, so Nomura saved him for the final door. Did you spot him in 2002?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Disney only let Mickey Mouse appear in one scene of the first Kingdom Hearts? The game launched in Japan on March 28, 2002, and reached North America that September. Disney first wanted the game built entirely around its own characters and worlds. Director Tetsuya Nomura pushed back and insisted on an original hero in an original universe. That hero became Sora. When it came to Mickey, the contract was strict. Nomura later explained in the Kingdom Hearts Ultimania book that contractual issues limited Mickey to a single scene. Disney offered a role like waving from the back of a crowd in town. Nomura decided that if he only got one shot, it should leave the biggest impression possible. So Mickey shows up at the very end, seen from behind, helping Sora close the door to Kingdom Hearts. Players barely saw his face, and it became one of the most talked about moments in the game. The gamble paid off. By April 2003 the game had sold 3 million copies around the world. By the end of 2006 it had shipped more than 5.6 million copies. Disney loosened up after that, and Mickey became a full character in the sequels. Did that final scene surprise you back in 2002? Follow for more gaming history.
